title: Twenty-three years
hook: it came in parts over about twenty-three years, as situations arose (17:106)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Qur'an: recitation, a voice before a page. Your line was the book is a voice. Did you read something aloud, and did it change? Day three hundred ten.

A letter arrives one paragraph at a time, over twenty-three years. Some paragraphs come when you're frightened. Some come the week you lose someone. Some come while your town is arguing about what's fair. Each one answers something happening right then, and together they make one letter. That's how Muslims describe the Qur'an arriving: not handed down as a finished book in a single night, but in parts, over about twenty-three years, from the cave of Hira to the last months of the Prophet's life. Today: twenty-three years.
screen: `A LETTER, ONE PARAGRAPH AT A TIME.` → `EACH ONE ANSWERS A MOMENT.` → `FROM THE CAVE TO THE LAST MONTHS.`

segments.voice: A report from Ibn Abbas in al-Bukhari gives the span: revelation began when the Prophet ﷺ was forty, and he lived thirteen years in Mecca, then ten in Medina, until he died. In between, verses arrived as situations arose: a question someone asked, a hardship, a dispute, a battle, a grief. The Qur'an says so itself. In Pickthall's words: "And (it is) a Qur'an that We have divided, that thou mayst recite it unto mankind at intervals, and We have revealed it by (successive) revelation." Another verse records people asking why it wasn't sent down all at once, and answers: so that the Prophet's heart would be made firm by it. Muslim scholars add a detail. A report from Ibn Abbas says the Qur'an came down whole to the nearest heaven on the Night of Power, and from there to the Prophet in parts. So Muslims speak of both: complete, and arriving slowly. And there's a reason people often give: gentleness. Aisha, the Prophet's wife, said the first things revealed were short surahs about paradise and the fire, and only once people's hearts had turned did the rules on what's allowed and forbidden come. If the first thing revealed had been do not drink wine, she said, people would have answered: we will never give it up. Scholars call the stories behind particular verses asbab al-nuzul, the occasions of revelation. A woman named Khawlah came to the Prophet about her husband's harsh treatment and argued her case, and the opening of Surah 58 came about her: Allah has heard the one who pleads with you. Not every verse has a known occasion, and scholars weigh those reports carefully. But the picture holds: a book that met people where they were, one piece at a time.
screen: `FROM THE CAVE TO HIS LAST YEAR` · `DIVIDED, TO RECITE AT INTERVALS` · `GENTLENESS FIRST, RULES LATER` · `THE OCCASIONS OF REVELATION`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: learn one verse's occasion, and hold it. Picture Khawlah: a woman with trouble at home, going to the Prophet, pleading her case, and being heard. The verse opens by saying her voice reached Allah. Now bring to mind one situation in your own life that you'd want answered. Don't solve it. Just hold it, the way she carried hers in. If you pray, you can bring it to Allah in your own words. The bell holds the time.
Twenty-three years. How long the Qur'an took to arrive: in parts, from the cave of Hira to the Prophet's last year, as life happened. Today's word.
Your line: it came slowly. Today, when something good in you is growing slowly, a habit, a skill, a healing, let it be slow, and take the one piece in front of you. Day three hundred ten.

howItsDone: Muslims teach that the Qur'an was revealed in parts over about twenty-three years, and students of the Qur'an learn the occasions of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) for many verses to understand them in their setting.

fork.setup: you're bringing a new message to people who love their old ways. what comes first?
options: the heart: God, the Day, paradise and the fire.

original.note: Arabic: the occasions (literally causes) of the coming down, the stories behind particular verses.

trapdoor: what you thought: a book that took a long time to write.
what it means: a book that arrived in parts over about twenty-three years, each part meeting a moment.
what a scholar hears: the Qur'an's own answer in 25:32, to make the Prophet's heart firm, and a whole science, asbab al-nuzul, handled with care because not every report is sound.

Dates: first revelation c. 610 CE (Prophet about 40), death 632 CE. Some reckon the span as 22 to 23 years; the index says about 23.
Bukhari 4993 numbering for Aisha's statement; confirm.
Ibn Abbas report of the descent to bayt al-'izzah on the Night of Power: confirm sources and grading.
